analyst.summary: Bharti Hexacom delivered a steady but unspectacular FY26 (revenue +9.4%, PAT +16.1%, 53% EBITDA margin), with Q4 FY26 reported profit down 4.6% YoY only because of a small one-off government-levy charge (core profit was actually +22.5%). ARPU growth (+4.1% YoY to Rs 252) is lapping the prior tariff hike rather than reflecting a new one, subscriber growth is modest (+3.6% YoY) on a maturing Rajasthan/North-East base, and the standout growth line is the still-small Homes/Office/FWA segment (+65.3% YoY). At ~45-46x trailing P/E against a cited sector average of ~17.6x and a DCF-implied fair-P/E estimate of ~34x, the stock is priced well ahead of its delivered growth rate, betting on either a fresh tariff hike or continued FWA-led re-rating -- neither confirmed yet. No balance-sheet or governance red flags surfaced. Quant score not yet computed; V1 default of Hold applies, with valuation richness flagged as the key watch-item into Bharti Airtel's Q1 FY27 print (expected early-to-mid August 2026, exact date PENDING).
